A battle bow hung up and turned away from humanity, signaling peace and mercy
A reminder to hunt wild beasts
A measurement of rainfall
questions.explanation: The rainbow resembles an archer's bow hung up in the sky, pointing away from earth, symbolizing God's disarmament and promise of peace.

questions.text: Which of the following is true regarding the conditions of the Noahic covenant?
options: It was completely unconditional; God promised preservation by pure grace regardless of future storms
It required all men to build an ark every hundred years
It terminated as soon as Noah passed away
It only protected those living in the Middle East
questions.explanation: God's covenant never again to destroy the whole earth with a flood was an unconditional commitment of divine grace and preservation.

questions.text: What did God establish as the fundamental basis for the capital prohibition of murder in Genesis 9?
options: The economic loss of productive labor
Man was created in the divine image and likeness of God
The king's personal pride
The scarcity of population
questions.explanation: Genesis 9:6 grounds the sacredness of human life in the imago Dei: 'for in the image of God He made man.'

questions.text: How many stories (decks) did the Ark of Noah have according to Genesis 6:16?
options: One single open deck
Two stories
Three stories (lower, second, and third decks)
Five stories
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:16: 'You shall make it with lower, second, and third decks.'

questions.text: How was illumination provided for the Ark according to Genesis 6:16?
options: Continuous burning torches
A window (opening for light) finished to a cubit from the top
Mirrors reflecting starlight
Clear crystal stones
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:16: 'You shall make a window for the ark, and you shall finish it to a cubit from above.'

questions.text: Who closed the door of the Ark after Noah, his family, and the animals entered?
options: Noah and his three sons
The Lord God shut him in
The local community who gathered outside
The angel Gabriel
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:16 explicitly notes: 'And the Lord shut him in.'

questions.text: How many days did the floodwaters prevail upon the earth before beginning to decrease?
options: Forty days
One hundred and fifty days
Three hundred days
Seventy days
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:24 states: 'And the waters prevailed on the earth one hundred and fifty days.'

questions.text: What caused the floodwaters to recede as recorded in Genesis 8:1?
options: Great heat from volcanic eruptions
God remembered Noah, and God made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subsided
The people built canals to the ocean
The clouds absorbed all the water
questions.explanation: Genesis 8:1: 'Then God remembered Noah... And God made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subsided.'

questions.text: Which of the following demonstrates that God does not abandon His creation after crisis?
options: The establishment of the Noahic covenant guaranteeing the rhythm of nature and seasons
The immediate extinction of all plant life
The prohibition of marriage
The requirement that man live in underground shelters
questions.explanation: God's covenant with Noah demonstrates His redemptive preservation and providential commitment to sustain the earth.

questions.text: Why did ancient covenants often include animal sacrifice and the shedding of blood during their ratification ceremony?
options: To provide a feast for the neighborhood
To solemnize the agreement with a life-and-death seal signifying the binding gravity of the vows
To appease local kings
To dispose of unwanted livestock
questions.explanation: Blood rituals signified that the covenant was a life-and-death commitment; breaking it invoked severe consequences.

questions.text: How does the Noahic covenant reflect God's sovereignty over the forces of nature?
options: It proves that weather patterns are completely uncontrollable by God
It shows that God alone controls the waters of the deep and the windows of heaven, setting boundaries for creation
It demonstrates that human prayers dictate the seasons
It indicates that angels manage the oceans independently
questions.explanation: God commanded the flood into being and subsequently set eternal limits on the waters, confirming His total sovereignty.

questions.text: In the sequence of divine covenants in scripture, the Noahic covenant serves as the foundation of:
options: Common grace and cosmic preservation for all living things
The Levitical priesthood
The Davidic monarchy in Jerusalem
The New Testament church hierarchy
questions.explanation: The Noahic covenant is the cornerstone of common grace, ensuring the stability of cosmic order so that God's redemptive plan can unfold.

questions.text: Where was Abraham originally living when God first called him into a covenant relationship?
options: In Ur of the Chaldeans in Mesopotamia
In Jerusalem on Mount Zion
In Alexandria in Egypt
In Damascus of Syria
questions.explanation: Abraham was born Abram, son of Terah, in the land of Ur of the Chaldeans in ancient Mesopotamia (Genesis 11:28, 31).

questions.text: Who was the father of Abraham according to Genesis 11:26?
options: Nahor
Terah
Haran
Lot
questions.explanation: Genesis 11:26 states: 'Now Terah lived seventy years, and begot Abram, Nahor, and Haran.'

questions.text: How old was Abraham when he departed from Haran in obedience to God's command?
options: 50 years old
75 years old
99 years old
100 years old
questions.explanation: Genesis 12:4: 'And Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran.'

questions.text: Whom did Abram take with him when he embarked on his journey of faith to Canaan?
options: His father Terah and all his brothers
His wife Sarai and his nephew Lot, along with their possessions and people
An army of three hundred soldiers
Only his servant Eliezer
questions.explanation: Genesis 12:5: 'Then Abram took Sarai his wife and Lot his brother’s son, and all their possessions that they had gathered...'

questions.text: Which of the following was NOT one of God's initial promises to Abram during his call in Genesis 12:1-3?
options: I will make you a great nation and bless you
I will make your name great and you will be a blessing
You will immediately be crowned King of Egypt
Through you all the families of the earth shall be blessed
questions.explanation: God promised a great nation, greatness of name, blessing, protection, and universal blessing, not kingship over Egypt.

questions.text: At which significant location in Canaan did God first appear to Abram and promise the land to his descendants?
options: At Bethel near the valley
At Shechem, by the Oak of Moreh
At Beersheba by the well
At Hebron near the cave
questions.explanation: Abram passed through the land to the place of Shechem, as far as the terebinth tree (Oak) of Moreh, where God appeared to him (Genesis 12:6-7).

questions.text: What did Abram do at Shechem in response to God's appearance and promise of the land?
options: He built a fortified stone wall
He built an altar to the Lord who had appeared to him
He declared war on the Canaanites
He dug a deep trench around the city
questions.explanation: Genesis 12:7: 'And there he built an altar to the Lord, who had appeared to him.'

questions.text: What caused the dispute between the herdsmen of Abram and the herdsmen of Lot in Genesis 13?
options: A disagreement over the price of wool
The land could not support them both because their livestock and possessions were so great
Lot wanted to worship Canaanite gods
Abram refused to share his tents
questions.explanation: Genesis 13:6-7 records that the land was not able to support them, for their possessions were so great; and there was strife between their herdsmen.

questions.text: How did Abram demonstrate generosity, humility, and peaceful leadership during the dispute with Lot?
options: He commanded Lot to leave the territory immediately
He allowed Lot, the younger man, the first choice of the entire land
He took the matter to the elders of Sodom
He divided the herds equally by force
questions.explanation: Abram selflessly offered Lot the choice: 'Please let there be no strife between you and me... If you take the left, then I will go to the right' (Genesis 13:8-9).

questions.text: Which region did Lot choose for himself, pitching his tent as far as Sodom?
options: The rugged hill country of Hebron
The fertile plain of the Jordan, well-watered everywhere
The coastal plains of Philistia
The arid wilderness of Sinai
questions.explanation: Lot saw all the plain of Jordan, that it was well watered everywhere like the garden of the Lord, and chose all the plain of Jordan toward Sodom (Genesis 13:10-12).

questions.text: After Lot separated from him, what promise did God renew to Abram in Genesis 13:14-17?
options: That he would conquer Egypt in his lifetime
All the land he could see in all four directions would be given to him and his descendants forever, as dust of the earth
That Lot would become his lifelong servant
That no rain would fall on the mountains
questions.explanation: The Lord said to Abram: 'Lift your eyes now... all the land which you see I give to you and your descendants forever' (Genesis 13:14-15).

questions.text: When Lot was captured during the war of the four kings against the five kings of Sodom, how did Abram respond?
options: He rejoiced that Lot had received his punishment
He armed his 318 trained servants, pursued the invaders to Dan, defeated them, and rescued Lot and his possessions
He sent a ransom letter to the king of Elam
He fled south toward Egypt
questions.explanation: Abram armed his 318 trained men born in his own house, pursued them, brought back all the goods, and also brought back his nephew Lot (Genesis 14:14-16).

questions.text: Why did Abram refuse to take any of the spoils of war offered by the King of Sodom in Genesis 14:22-24?
options: Because the goods were stolen from Egypt
Lest the king of Sodom should boast, 'I have made Abram rich'
Because Abram had no storage wagons
Because Melchizedek forbade him
questions.explanation: Abram declared to the king of Sodom that he would not take even a thread or sandal strap, 'lest you should say, "I have made Abram rich"' (Genesis 14:23).

questions.text: Who met Abram returning from the slaughter of the kings, bringing bread and wine and blessing him?
options: Abimelech king of Gerar
Melchizedek king of Salem and priest of God Most High
Pharaoh king of Egypt
Jethro priest of Midian
questions.explanation: Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine; he was the priest of God Most High, and Abram gave him a tithe of all (Genesis 14:18-20).

questions.text: When Abram lamented that he was childless and that Eliezer of Damascus would be his heir, what did God promise him?
options: Eliezer would be his spiritual adopted son
One who will come from your own body shall be your heir, and your descendants shall be as numerous as the stars
Lot would inherit all his property
He would adopt twelve sons from Haran
questions.explanation: God brought Abram outside and said: 'Look now toward heaven, and count the stars... So shall your descendants be.' And Abram believed the Lord (Genesis 15:4-5).

questions.text: According to Genesis 15:6, how did God view Abram's faith when he believed the promise of descendants?
options: It was accounted to him for righteousness
It was viewed as wishful thinking
It was tested with heavy taxation
It was considered unnecessary
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:6: 'And he believed in the Lord, and He accounted it to him for righteousness.'

questions.text: In Genesis 15:13-14, God foretold that Abram's descendants would be strangers and enslaved in a foreign land for:
options: 40 years
100 years
400 years
1000 years
questions.explanation: God revealed that his descendants would be afflicted four hundred years, after which God would judge that nation and bring them out with great possessions.

questions.text: Because Sarai remained barren, what human initiative did she propose to Abram in Genesis 16?
options: To adopt children from the Canaanite tribes
To sleep with her Egyptian maidservant Hagar to obtain children through her
To return to Haran permanently
To make sacrifices at Sodom
questions.explanation: Sarai said to Abram: 'See now, the Lord has restrained me from bearing children. Please, go in to my maid; perhaps I shall obtain children by her' (Genesis 16:2).

questions.text: What was the name of the son born to Abram through the Egyptian maidservant Hagar?
options: Isaac
Ishmael
Midian
Esau
questions.explanation: Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram named his son, whom Hagar bore, Ishmael (Genesis 16:15).

questions.text: How old was Abram when Ishmael was born to him by Hagar?
options: 75 years old
80 years old
86 years old
99 years old
questions.explanation: Genesis 16:16 states: 'Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram.'

questions.text: How old was Abraham when the Lord appeared to him to establish the covenant of circumcision in Genesis 17?
options: 86 years old
90 years old
99 years old
100 years old
questions.explanation: Genesis 17:1: 'When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the Lord appeared to Abram and said to him, "I am Almighty God; walk before Me and be blameless."'

questions.text: What fundamental moral requirement did God demand of Abraham in Genesis 17:1?
options: Offer ten oxen every Sabbath
Walk before Me and be blameless
Conquer seven nations in war
Build a temple of cedar
questions.explanation: God declared: 'I am Almighty God (El Shaddai); walk before Me and be blameless' (Genesis 17:1).

questions.text: What was the spiritual significance of changing the name 'Abram' (exalted father) to 'Abraham'?
options: It symbolized his promotion to Egyptian nobility
It signified that God had made him the father of many nations
It indicated his advanced old age
It showed he had moved from Haran to Canaan
questions.explanation: Genesis 17:5: 'No longer shall your name be called Abram, but your name shall be Abraham; for I have made you a father of many nations.'

questions.text: What was the physical sign and seal instituted by God for the Abrahamic covenant in Genesis 17?
options: A rainbow across the sky
Circumcision of the foreskin of every male child
Wearing a blue tassel on garments
Sprinkling animal blood on the doorposts
questions.explanation: Genesis 17:10-11: 'This is My covenant which you shall keep... Every male child among you shall be circumcised... it shall be a sign of the covenant between Me and you.'

questions.text: On which specific day of life was every newborn male in Abraham's household to be circumcised?
options: On the third day
On the seventh day
On the eighth day
On the fortieth day
questions.explanation: Genesis 17:12: 'He who is eight days old among you shall be circumcised, every male child in your generations.'

questions.text: What serious consequence was declared for any uncircumcised male in Abraham's household?
options: He had to pay twenty shekels of silver
That soul shall be cut off from his people; he has broken God's covenant
He was made a slave for seven years
He was banished to the desert alone
questions.explanation: Genesis 17:14: 'And the uncircumcised male child... that person shall be cut off from his people; he has broken My covenant.'

questions.text: To what was Sarai's name changed by God in Genesis 17:15, and what was her promise?
options: Hagar; mother of servants
Sarah; she shall be a mother of nations and kings of peoples shall come from her
Milcah; queen of the desert
Keturah; ruler of wealth
questions.explanation: Genesis 17:15-16: 'As for Sarai your wife, you shall not call her name Sarai, but Sarah shall be her name. And I will bless her and also give you a son by her...'

questions.text: How did Abraham react when God announced that Sarah would give birth to a son in her old age?
options: He fell on his face and laughed in amazement
He grew furious and rejected the prophecy
He immediately divorced Sarah
He called for his Egyptian doctors
questions.explanation: Genesis 17:17: 'Then Abraham fell on his face and laughed, and said in his heart, "Shall a child be born to a man who is one hundred years old? And shall Sarah, who is ninety years old, bear a child?"'

questions.text: What plea did Abraham make on behalf of his firstborn son Ishmael in Genesis 17:18?
options: Make Ishmael the high priest of Salem
Oh, that Ishmael might live before You!
Let Ishmael conquer the land of Canaan
Give Ishmael all of Sarah's gold
questions.explanation: Genesis 17:18: 'And Abraham said to God, "Oh, that Ishmael might live before You!"'

questions.text: What specific name did God command Abraham to give to Sarah's promised son, and why?
options: Jacob, because he will struggle
Isaac, meaning laughter
Joseph, because God will add
Moses, drawn out of water
questions.explanation: God said: 'No, Sarah your wife shall bear you a son, and you shall call his name Isaac; I will establish My covenant with him for an everlasting covenant' (Genesis 17:19).

questions.text: What promise did God make regarding Ishmael in Genesis 17:20?
options: He would inherit the land of Canaan
He would be blessed, become exceedingly fruitful, and beget twelve princes as a great nation
He would serve Isaac as a bondsman forever
He would become the king of Egypt
questions.explanation: Genesis 17:20: 'And as for Ishmael, I have heard you. Behold, I have blessed him, and will make him fruitful... He shall beget twelve princes, and I will make him a great nation.'

questions.text: With whom did God definitively confirm His everlasting covenant would be established?
options: With Ishmael only
With Eliezer of Damascus
With Isaac, whom Sarah would bear at that set time next year
With Lot's descendants in Moab
questions.explanation: Genesis 17:21: 'But My covenant I will establish with Isaac, whom Sarah shall bear to you at this set time next year.'

questions.text: When did Abraham carry out the rite of circumcision on himself, Ishmael, and all males of his house?
options: Ten years later after returning to Ur
That very same day, as God had said to him
Only after Isaac was born
After consulting with the Canaanite kings
questions.explanation: Genesis 17:23: 'So Abraham took Ishmael his son, all who were born in his house... and circumcised the flesh of their foreskins that very same day, as God had said to him.'

questions.text: How old was Abraham when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin?
options: 75 years old
86 years old
99 years old
100 years old
questions.explanation: Genesis 17:24: 'Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.'

questions.text: How old was Ishmael when he was circumcised alongside his father Abraham?
options: 8 days old
12 years old
13 years old
20 years old
questions.explanation: Genesis 17:25: 'And Ishmael his son was thirteen years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.'

questions.text: The Abrahamic covenant marks the foundational beginning in biblical history of:
options: The formal revelation of God's covenant of grace to save a people for Himself
The system of animal sacrifices in the tabernacle
Monarchy and civil government in the ancient Near East
The writing of the Torah on papyrus
questions.explanation: The Abrahamic covenant is the cornerstone of redemptive history, revealing God's gracious election of a covenant people through faith.

questions.text: Which two major physical obstacles stood against Abraham's hope of having a biological son with Sarah?
options: Famine in the land and war with Philistines
Their extreme old age and Sarah's lifelong barrenness
Opposition from Egyptian Pharaohs and tribal raids
Poverty and lack of cattle
questions.explanation: Humanly speaking, Sarah was barren and well past childbearing age (90 years old), and Abraham was ninety-nine, making conception biologically miraculous.

questions.text: In the New Testament (Romans 4 and Galatians 3), Abraham is celebrated primarily as the father of:
options: Military conquest
All those who believe and have faith in God
Architectural design
Egyptian statecraft
questions.explanation: Paul describes Abraham as the spiritual father of all who walk in the footsteps of faith (Romans 4:11-16; Galatians 3:7-9).

questions.text: What lesson concerning God's promises can Christians learn from the birth of Isaac after twenty-five years of waiting?
options: God's delays mean divine unfaithfulness
God always fulfills His promises in His own perfect timing, for nothing is too hard for Him
Human shortcuts are superior to divine patience
Faith is unnecessary once a promise is uttered
questions.explanation: The story demonstrates that God is entirely trustworthy, capable of fulfilling what seems impossible in human eyes.

questions.text: What territory was specifically designated by God as the 'land of Canaan' promised to Abraham's seed?
options: The land of his sojourning, from the river of Egypt to the great river Euphrates
The entire delta of the Nile in Egypt
The mountains of Ararat and Media
The island of Crete
questions.explanation: Genesis 15:18 and 17:8 outline the promised territory given to Abraham's offspring, extending from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates.

questions.text: Why did God demand the physical cutting of circumcision as the covenant sign?
options: To serve as an Egyptian medical treatment
As a permanent bodily reminder of consecration, cutting off of fleshly self-reliance, and dedication to God
To mark soldiers for military service
To identify tax-paying citizens
questions.explanation: Circumcision was an indelible sign in the body signifying belonging to Yahweh, holy separation, and reliance on divine promise rather than human flesh.

questions.text: What was Abraham's immediate response when God called him in Haran to leave his country and kindred?
options: He demanded a written sign and proof
He obeyed promptly in faith, not knowing where he was going
He consulted with the local pagan priests
He asked to delay his departure by twenty years
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:8 praises Abraham: 'By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to go out to the place which he would receive as an inheritance. And he went out, not knowing where he was going.'

questions.text: Which of the following demonstrates that Abraham was wealthy in possessions during his sojourns?
options: He owned a fleet of Mediterranean ships
He had great flocks, herds, silver, gold, and 318 trained servants
He minted his own bronze coins
He established a palace in Babylon
questions.explanation: Genesis 13:2 notes: 'Abram was very rich in livestock, in silver, and in gold', and 14:14 records his 318 armed household servants.

questions.text: What title did Melchizedek bestow upon the Lord God when blessing Abram in Genesis 14:19?
options: God of the underworld
God Most High (El Elyon), Possessor of heaven and earth
Sun-god of the morning
Deity of the river Jordan
questions.explanation: Melchizedek blessed him and said: 'Blessed be Abram of God Most High, Possessor of heaven and earth' (Genesis 14:19).

questions.text: In Genesis 15, how did God confirm His covenant promise to Abram through a solemn ceremony?
options: By shaking hands before the city gate
By passing between the divided halves of sacrificed animals as a smoking oven and burning torch
By erecting twelve stone monuments on the shore
By pouring olive oil over Abram's head
questions.explanation: In an ancient covenant cutting ritual, God alone passed between the pieces as a smoking oven and burning torch, swearing His unilateral faithfulness (Genesis 15:17).

questions.text: What interpersonal conflict arose in Abraham's household after Hagar conceived Ishmael?
options: Hagar despised her mistress Sarah, leading to harsh treatment and Hagar fleeing to the wilderness
Lot demanded that Hagar marry one of his herdsmen
The servants staged a rebellion against Abraham
Sarah left the camp and moved to Sodom
questions.explanation: When Hagar saw that she had conceived, her mistress became despised in her eyes, creating household turmoil (Genesis 16:4-6).

questions.text: What well in the wilderness was named by Hagar because the Angel of the Lord saw and comforted her?
options: Beer-lahai-roi (the well of the One who lives and sees me)
Beersheba (well of the oath)
Meribah (well of contention)
Marah (well of bitterness)
questions.explanation: Hagar called the name of the Lord who spoke to her 'You-Are-the-God-Who-Sees', and the well was called Beer-lahai-roi (Genesis 16:13-14).

questions.text: What does the Latin/theological phrase 'ex nihilo' and God's call to Abraham teach about divine power?
options: God only works when human beings provide strong foundations
God calls into existence things that do not exist, transforming human impossibility into reality
God depends on astrologers to choose righteous men
Divine power is restricted to natural laws
questions.explanation: Romans 4:17 describes God as the One 'who gives life to the dead and calls those things which do not exist as though they did.'

questions.text: Why did God initiate the covenant with Abraham rather than Abraham seeking God first?
options: Because Abraham had performed great miracles in Ur
Because of God's sovereign grace and divine election, choosing Abraham from an idolatrous background
Because Terah requested God to mentor his son
Because Mesopotamia had no temples
questions.explanation: The Abrahamic covenant demonstrates sovereign grace; God initiated contact with Abraham whose ancestors had served other gods (Joshua 24:2).

questions.text: How does the covenant promise 'in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed' find its ultimate fulfillment?
options: In the commercial trade routes of ancient Israel
In the coming of Jesus Christ, who brings salvation and eternal life to all nations
In the military victories of King David
In the building of Solomon's palace
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:8, 16 reveals that the ultimate fulfillment of the blessing to all nations is found in Jesus Christ, the promised seed of Abraham.

questions.text: How old was Abraham when his promised son Isaac was born to him by Sarah?
options: 75 years old
86 years old
99 years old
100 years old
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:5 states: 'Now Abraham was one hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.'

questions.text: What joyful exclamation did Sarah make at the birth and weaning of Isaac?
options: I have bought a son with silver
God has made laughter for me, and everyone who hears will laugh with me
My name shall be praised in Egypt
I am now equal to the angels
questions.explanation: Genesis 21:6 records Sarah saying: 'God has made laughter for me, and all who hear will laugh with me.'

questions.text: To test Abraham's absolute faith and obedience, what difficult command did God give him in Genesis 22?
options: Give all his cattle to the king of Sodom
Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love, and offer him as a burnt offering in the land of Moriah
Return to Ur of the Chaldees immediately
Build a tower of stone on Mount Carmel
questions.explanation: Genesis 22:2: 'Take now your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah, and offer him there as a burnt offering...'

questions.text: When Isaac asked his father on Mount Moriah, 'Look, the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?', what did Abraham answer?
options: We will catch a gazelle in the forest
My son, God will provide for Himself the lamb for a burnt offering
You are the lamb for the sacrifice
An angel will carry the wood back
questions.explanation: Abraham replied with prophetic faith: 'My son, God will provide for Himself the lamb for a burnt offering' (Genesis 22:8).

questions.text: Just as Abraham stretched out his hand and took the knife to slay his son, who called to him from heaven?
options: The Angel of the Lord
Melchizedek
Sarah
Lot
questions.explanation: Genesis 22:11: 'But the Angel of the Lord called to him from heaven and said, "Abraham, Abraham!" And he said, "Here I am."'

questions.text: What divine substitute did God provide caught in a nearby thicket by its horns for the sacrifice?
options: A young bull
A ram
A female goat
A white dove
questions.explanation: Genesis 22:13: 'Then Abraham lifted his eyes and looked, and there behind him was a ram caught in a thicket by its horns.'

questions.text: What memorable name did Abraham give to the place on Mount Moriah where God provided the sacrifice?
options: Jehovah Nissi (The Lord is my banner)
Jehovah Jireh (The Lord will provide)
Jehovah Shalom (The Lord is peace)
Jehovah Rapha (The Lord heals)
questions.explanation: Abraham called the name of the place 'The-Lord-Will-Provide' (Jehovah Jireh); as it is said to this day, 'In the Mount of the Lord it shall be provided' (Genesis 22:14).

questions.text: What solemn oath did God swear to Abraham following his willingness not to withhold his only son?
options: He would give Abraham kingship over Syria
Blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply your descendants as the stars of the heaven and the sand on the seashore
Isaac would never face any family hardships
Ishmael would become the high priest of Canaan
questions.explanation: Genesis 22:16-17: 'By Myself I have sworn, says the Lord, because you have done this thing... blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply your descendants...'

questions.text: When Abraham sent his trusted senior servant (Eliezer) to find a wife for Isaac, where did he instruct him to go?
options: To the daughters of the Canaanites in Hebron
To Abraham's own country and kindred in Mesopotamia (Haran)
To the royal court of the Pharaoh in Egypt
To the land of the Philistines in Gerar
questions.explanation: Abraham charged his servant: 'you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites... but you shall go to my country and to my family' (Genesis 24:3-4).

questions.text: What prayer sign did Abraham's servant ask of God at the well of water outside the city of Nahor?
options: That the maiden would offer him a golden bowl of wine
That the young woman who offers to draw water for him and his ten camels also would be the chosen bride for Isaac
That an angel would appear standing on the well
That the well water would miraculously turn sweet
questions.explanation: Eliezer prayed that when he asked for a drink, the maiden who answered, 'Drink, and I will give your camels a drink also' would be the one appointed for Isaac (Genesis 24:14).

questions.text: Who fulfilled the servant's prayer by running to the well and drawing water for all his camels?
options: Rachel
Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel son of Milcah
Leah
Zipporah
questions.explanation: Before he had finished speaking, Rebekah came out with her pitcher on her shoulder, gave him drink, and drew water for all his camels (Genesis 24:15-20).

questions.text: When Rebekah was barren for many years, what did Isaac do, and how did God respond?
options: He took a second wife from the Hittites
He pleaded with the Lord for his wife, and the Lord granted his plea so Rebekah conceived
He returned to Egypt to consult physicians
He gave up hope of having descendants
questions.explanation: Genesis 25:21: 'Now Isaac pleaded with the Lord for his wife, because she was barren; and the Lord granted his plea, and Rebekah his wife conceived.'

questions.text: What prophecy did God reveal to Rebekah concerning the twin boys struggling in her womb?
options: Both sons will die in infancy
Two nations are in your womb... and the older shall serve the younger
The firstborn will rule with iron chariots
They will establish one single tribe
questions.explanation: The Lord said to her: 'Two nations are in your womb, two peoples shall be separated from your body; one people shall be stronger than the other, and the older shall serve the younger' (Genesis 25:23).

questions.text: Name the twin sons born to Isaac and Rebekah:
options: Joseph and Benjamin
Esau and Jacob
Ephraim and Manasseh
Perez and Zerah
questions.explanation: The first came out red and hairy like a garment, named Esau; afterward his brother came out with his hand holding Esau's heel, named Jacob (Genesis 25:25-26).

questions.text: Which of the twin sons of Isaac was chosen in the covenant lineage to become the father of the twelve tribes of Israel?
options: Esau (Edom)
Jacob (Israel)
Both equally
Neither son
questions.explanation: God confirmed the covenant of Abraham and Isaac with Jacob, renaming him Israel, the father of the twelve tribes.

questions.text: According to Exodus 2:23-25, what prompted God to initiate Israel's deliverance from Egyptian slavery?
options: The Pharaoh sent an official petition to God
The children of Israel groaned because of the bondage and cried out, and God remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
The Nile dried up completely
Moses requested an army from Midian
questions.explanation: Exodus 2:24: 'So God heard their groaning, and God remembered His covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.'

questions.text: How long had the descendants of Jacob resided in Egypt before the Exodus deliverance?
options: 40 years
120 years
Over 400 to 430 years
70 years
questions.explanation: Exodus 12:40 notes that the sojourn of the children of Israel who lived in Egypt was four hundred and thirty years.

questions.text: At what point in their journey after leaving Egypt did the children of Israel arrive at the wilderness of Sinai?
options: In the first week
In the third month after they had gone out of the land of Egypt
After two full years
On the seventh day
questions.explanation: Exodus 19:1: 'In the third month after the children of Israel had gone out of the land of Egypt, on the same day, they came to the Wilderness of Sinai.'

questions.text: What majestic offer of covenant relationship did God proclaim to Israel through Moses at Mount Sinai in Exodus 19:5-6?
options: If you obey My voice and keep My covenant, you shall be a special treasure above all people, a kingdom of priests and a holy nation
You shall conquer all continents and become merchants of gold
You shall return to Egypt as masters
You will never have to keep any moral laws
questions.explanation: Exodus 19:5-6: 'Now therefore, if you will indeed obey My voice and keep My covenant, then you shall be a special treasure to Me above all people... a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.'

questions.text: What was the unanimous response of the elders and people of Israel to God's proposal in Exodus 19:8?
options: We need thirty days to consult with our families
All that the Lord has spoken we will do!
Moses must keep the covenant on our behalf alone
We prefer to return to Goshen
questions.explanation: Exodus 19:8: 'Then all the people answered together and said, "All that the Lord has spoken we will do."'

questions.text: How did God instruct Moses to prepare the people before He descended on Mount Sinai?
options: Build a fleet of wooden chariots
Consecrate them today and tomorrow, let them wash their clothes, and be ready for the third day
Fast from all food and water for seven days
Erect a stone temple at the base of the mountain
questions.explanation: The Lord said to Moses: 'Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their clothes. And let them be ready for the third day' (Exodus 19:10-11).

questions.text: What physical boundary rule was placed around Mount Sinai during the revelation of God?
options: Anyone could climb freely at sunrise
Whoever touches the mountain, whether beast or man, shall surely be put to death
Only the priests could dance on the slopes
A trench was filled with oil
questions.explanation: Exodus 19:12-13: 'Take heed to yourselves that you do not go up to the mountain or touch its base. Whoever touches the mountain shall surely be put to death.'

questions.text: What atmospheric and supernatural manifestations occurred when the Lord descended on Mount Sinai on the third day?
options: Gentle warm rain and singing birds
Thunder, lightning, a thick cloud, the voice of an exceedingly loud trumpet, smoke like a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked violently
A quiet breeze without any sound
Total darkness lasting thirty days
questions.explanation: Exodus 19:16-18 describes thunderings and lightnings, a thick cloud, an exceedingly loud trumpet, smoke ascending like a furnace, and violent shaking.

questions.text: What central legal and moral code did God speak to Israel from Mount Sinai in Exodus 20?
options: The Code of Hammurabi
The Ten Commandments (Decalogue)
The laws of the Roman senate
The proverbs of ancient Egypt
questions.explanation: Exodus 20 records the revelation of the Ten Commandments, the moral core of the Sinai covenant.

questions.text: What is the first of the Ten Commandments given in Exodus 20:2-3?
options: Honor your father and mother
You shall have no other gods before Me
Remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy
You shall not make any graven image
questions.explanation: Exodus 20:3: 'You shall have no other gods before Me.'

questions.text: Which commandment prohibits creating and bowing down to any carved image or likeness of anything in heaven or earth?
options: The first commandment
The second commandment
The third commandment
The fourth commandment
questions.explanation: The second commandment (Exodus 20:4-5) forbids making idols or carved images and bowing down to serve them.

questions.text: Which commandment commands believers not to take the name of the Lord God in vain?
options: The second commandment
The third commandment
The fifth commandment
The seventh commandment
questions.explanation: Exodus 20:7: 'You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain, for the Lord will not hold him guiltless who takes His name in vain.'

questions.text: What is the fourth commandment concerning the weekly cycle of work and rest?
options: Work seven days without resting
Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy; six days you shall labor, but the seventh day is the Sabbath of the Lord
Fast every sixth day of the month
Rest on the first day of every month
questions.explanation: Exodus 20:8-10 commands keeping the Sabbath holy, commemorating God resting on the seventh day from all His creative works.

questions.text: Which commandment contains a specific promise: 'that your days may be long upon the land which the Lord your God is giving you'?
options: Fourth commandment
Fifth commandment: Honor your father and your mother
Sixth commandment
Eighth commandment
questions.explanation: Exodus 20:12: 'Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long upon the land which the Lord your God is giving you.'

questions.text: The prohibition 'You shall not murder' is which commandment in the Decalogue?
options: Fifth commandment
Sixth commandment
Seventh commandment
Ninth commandment
questions.explanation: Exodus 20:13: 'You shall not murder' (sixth commandment).

questions.text: Which commandments protect marital fidelity, property, and truthful testimony in society?
options: The first, second, and third commandments
Seventh (no adultery), Eighth (no stealing), and Ninth (no false witness)
The fifth and sixth commandments only
The tenth commandment only
questions.explanation: Exodus 20:14-16 protects marriage (7th: no adultery), property (8th: no stealing), and truth/justice (9th: no false witness).

questions.text: What does the tenth commandment specifically address that distinguishes it from outward actions?
options: It regulates taxation
It addresses internal desire and covetousness of a neighbor's house, wife, servants, or property
It requires animal sacrifice
It commands military training
questions.explanation: Exodus 20:17 strikes at the heart attitude: 'You shall not covet your neighbor’s house; you shall not covet your neighbor’s wife... nor anything that is your neighbor’s.'

questions.text: Why did the terrified Israelites ask Moses to speak to them instead of God speaking directly (Exodus 20:19)?
options: They could not hear God's voice
They feared that if God continued to speak to them directly in such majesty, they would die
They wanted to sleep in their tents
Moses had better oratorical skills
questions.explanation: Exodus 20:19: 'Then they said to Moses, "You speak with us, and we will hear; but let not God speak with us, lest we die."'

questions.text: In Exodus 24:1-2, whom did God instruct to come up toward the mountain to worship from afar?
options: All the armies of Israel
Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel
The kings of Edom and Moab
Only the young men who were unmarried
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:1: 'Now He said to Moses, "Come up to the Lord, you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel, and worship from afar."'

questions.text: What memorial structure did Moses build at the foot of Mount Sinai during the covenant ceremony in Exodus 24:4?
options: A golden statue of a lion
An altar and twelve pillars according to the twelve tribes of Israel
A wooden fortress with towers
A stone archway inscribed with Egyptian hieroglyphs
questions.explanation: Moses rose early in the morning, and built an altar at the foot of the mountain, and twelve pillars according to the twelve tribes of Israel (Exodus 24:4).

questions.text: What sacrifices were offered by young men of Israel to seal the Sinai covenant?
options: Burnt offerings and peace offerings of oxen to the Lord
Turtledoves and pigeons only
Grain and honey cakes
Incense brought from Midian
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:5: 'Then he sent young men of the children of Israel, who offered burnt offerings and sacrificed peace offerings of oxen to the Lord.'

questions.text: What did Moses do with the blood of the sacrificed oxen during the ratification ceremony?
options: He poured it entirely into a trench and buried it
He put half the blood in basins and sprinkled it on the altar, and after reading the Book of the Covenant, sprinkled the remaining blood on the people
He burned the blood over cedar wood
He carried the blood into the desert
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:6-8: Moses sprinkled half on the altar and half on the people, declaring: 'This is the blood of the covenant which the Lord has made with you...'

questions.text: What did Moses declare as he sprinkled the blood on the congregation of Israel?
options: This is the sign of peace with Egypt
This is the blood of the covenant which the Lord has made with you according to all these words
May you prosper in cattle and sheep
We are now free from all commandments
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:8: 'And Moses took the blood, sprinkled it on the people, and said, "This is the blood of the covenant which the Lord has made with you..."'

questions.text: What extraordinary vision did Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and the seventy elders experience on the mountain in Exodus 24:9-11?
options: They saw an army of horses with wings
They saw the God of Israel, and under His feet was like a paved work of sapphire stone, clear as the heavens, and they ate and drank
They saw the city of Jericho destroyed
They saw a river of milk and honey
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:10-11 describes them seeing the God of Israel with sapphire pavement under His feet, and God did not lay a hand on them; they saw God, and they ate and drank in covenant fellowship.

questions.text: For how many days and nights was Moses on Mount Sinai receiving the tablets of stone and the commandments from God?
options: Seven days and seven nights
Twelve days and nights
Forty days and forty nights
Seventy days and nights
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:18: 'Moses went into the midst of the cloud and went up into the mountain. And Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights.'

questions.text: Who accompanied Moses partway up the mountain as his faithful minister?
options: Eleazar
Joshua
Caleb
Hur
questions.explanation: Exodus 24:13: 'So Moses arose with his assistant Joshua, and Moses went up to the mountain of God.'

questions.text: Whom did Moses leave in charge of resolving disputes among the people while he was on the mountain?
options: Eleazar and Phinehas
Aaron and Hur
Gershom and Eliezer
Joshua and Caleb
questions.explanation: Moses said to the elders: 'Wait here for us until we come back to you. Indeed, Aaron and Hur are with you. If any man has a difficulty, let him go to them' (Exodus 24:14).

questions.text: On what material were the Ten Commandments originally inscribed by the finger of God (Exodus 31:18)?
options: Parchment scrolls of sheepskin
Two tablets of stone
Plates of beaten gold
Wooden tablets of acacia
questions.explanation: Exodus 31:18 states that God gave Moses 'two tablets of the Testimony, tablets of stone, written with the finger of God.'

questions.text: What was the primary divine purpose of establishing the covenant at Mount Sinai with Israel?
options: To prepare them for trade with Greece and Rome
To separate Israel as God's holy, priestly people, distinguished from pagan nations by obedience to Yahweh
To make them wealthy landowners in Egypt
To abolish all future animal sacrifices
questions.explanation: The Sinai covenant formed the religious, moral, and civil identity of Israel as a consecrated nation belonging exclusively to Yahweh.

questions.text: What central theme underlies the relationship between God and Israel in the Mosaic covenant?
options: Commercial enrichment
Obedience to God's commandments leading to life and blessing, while disobedience brings curses and judgment
Passive philosophical contemplation
Total political expansion across Africa
questions.explanation: The covenant is conditional upon obedience: keeping the covenant brings divine protection and fruitfulness, while breaking it brings severe consequences (Deut 30:15-20).

questions.text: The sprinkling of blood upon the altar and the people at Mount Sinai symbolized:
options: An irreversible bond of life, cleansing, and mutual commitment between God and the nation
A declaration of war against surrounding nations
The end of the priesthood
Payment of taxes to Aaron
questions.explanation: Sprinkling half on the altar (representing God) and half on the people united them in a sacred, life-binding covenant sealed by blood.

questions.text: How does the Sinai covenant relate to the earlier covenant God made with Abraham?
options: Sinai completely abolished and cancelled the Abrahamic promises
Sinai was the historical progression and national fulfillment of God's promise to make Abraham's seed a great nation and give them Canaan
Sinai was formed by an entirely different deity
Sinai only applied to non-descendants of Abraham
questions.explanation: God explicitly remembered His Abrahamic covenant in Egypt and brought the children of Abraham to Sinai to organize them into the promised nation.

questions.text: Why is the Sinai covenant classified as a 'suzerainty covenant'?
options: Because Israel and God negotiated terms as equal kings
Because Yahweh, the supreme King and Sovereign Creator, established the stipulations, promised protection, and demanded total allegiance from His vassal people
Because Pharaoh signed the treaty as mediator
Because the covenant was written on two equal papyrus scrolls
questions.explanation: In suzerainty treaties of the ancient world, the great King initiated terms, delivered the vassal, and commanded undivided loyalty, perfectly mirroring Yahweh and Israel.

questions.text: What lesson from Abraham's willingness to sacrifice Isaac on Mount Moriah applies to Christian discipleship today?
options: Believers must offer human sacrifices to prove their faith
True faith holds nothing back from God, trusting that He will provide and can even raise the dead
Family relationships are more important than obeying God
God's promises always fail when tested
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:17-19 notes that Abraham believed God was able to raise Isaac up even from the dead; supreme love for God supersedes all earthly treasures.

questions.text: How does the sacrifice of the ram in place of Isaac foreshadow the New Testament gospel?
options: It proves that animal sacrifice was never pleasing to God
It prefigures Jesus Christ, the Lamb of God, who was offered as a substitute to die in the place of sinners
It shows that Isaac was unfit for leadership
It indicates that Mount Moriah should never be visited again
questions.explanation: The ram provided by God as a substitute for Isaac typifies the substitutionary atonement of Jesus Christ, providing redemption for mankind on Calvary.

questions.text: When Moses delayed in coming down from Mount Sinai, what demand did the Israelites make of Aaron in Exodus 32:1?
options: Appoint seventy new judges to rule over us
Come, make us gods that shall go before us; for as for this Moses, we do not know what has become of him
Lead us immediately into the land of Canaan
Collect bread and meat from the desert
questions.explanation: Exodus 32:1 records that the people gathered to Aaron and demanded: 'Come, make us gods that shall go before us; for as for this Moses, the man who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has become of him.'

questions.text: What did Aaron instruct the people to bring to him to fashion the idol in Exodus 32:2?
options: Silver coins from their travel bags
Golden earrings from the ears of their wives, sons, and daughters
Bronze mirrors used in Egypt
Acacia wood carved into statues
questions.explanation: Aaron said to them: 'Break off the golden earrings which are in the ears of your wives, your sons, and your daughters, and bring them to me' (Exodus 32:2).

questions.text: What form did Aaron fashion from the melted gold ornaments?
options: A winged serpent
A molded calf
A roaring lion
A golden sun-disk
questions.explanation: Aaron received the gold from their hand, fashioned it with an engraving tool, and made a molded calf (Exodus 32:4).

questions.text: What idolatrous proclamation did the Israelites shout when the golden calf was presented?
options: This is our king whom Aaron has chosen!
This is your god, O Israel, that brought you out of the land of Egypt!
Moses has sent this image from the mountain!
Let us bow down to the gods of Midian!
questions.explanation: The people declared: 'This is your god, O Israel, that brought you out of the land of Egypt!' (Exodus 32:4).

questions.text: How did Aaron compound the sin of the golden calf in Exodus 32:5?
options: He ordered everyone who refused to bow to be stoned
He built an altar before it and proclaimed, 'Tomorrow is a feast to the Lord'
He declared himself King of Egypt
He hid the calf inside the tent of meeting
questions.explanation: When Aaron saw it, he built an altar before it and made a proclamation: 'Tomorrow is a feast to the Lord' (Exodus 32:5).

questions.text: What behavior did the Israelites exhibit during the festival before the golden calf?
options: They wept in sackcloth and ashes
They rose up early, offered burnt offerings, sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play
They recited the Ten Commandments
They marched quietly around the mountain
questions.explanation: Exodus 32:6: 'Then they rose early on the next day, offered burnt offerings... the people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.'

questions.text: What did God propose to do to Israel when He saw their idolatry at the foot of the mountain?
options: Send them back to Pharaoh as slaves
Consume them in His wrath and make of Moses a great nation
Deprive them of water for forty days
Appoint Aaron as supreme monarch
questions.explanation: The Lord said to Moses: 'Now therefore, let Me alone, that My wrath may burn hot against them and I may consume them. And I will make of you a great nation' (Exodus 32:10).

questions.text: On what two powerful grounds did Moses intercede with God to turn away His wrath against Israel?
options: Israel's future military might and wealth
God's reputation before the Egyptians ('Why should the Egyptians say, He brought them out with evil intent?') and His sworn covenant to Abraham, Isaac, and Israel
Aaron's innocence and the children's youth
The value of the golden earrings
questions.explanation: Moses pleaded for God's holy name among the heathen and appealed to His unconditional oath to the patriarchs (Exodus 32:11-13).

questions.text: What was God's merciful response to Moses' heartfelt intercession in Exodus 32:14?
options: The Lord struck Moses with illness
The Lord relented from the destruction which He said He would do to His people
God abandoned the Israelites in the wilderness
God immediately took away Moses' leadership
questions.explanation: Exodus 32:14: 'So the Lord relented from the harm which He said He would do to His people.'

questions.text: When Moses and Joshua came down the mountain and heard the noise, what did Joshua mistake the sound for?
options: Singing of maidens
The noise of war in the camp
Thunder from the mountaintop
Lions roaring in the wilderness
questions.explanation: Exodus 32:17: 'And when Joshua heard the noise of the people as they shouted, he said to Moses, "There is a noise of war in the camp."'

questions.text: What did Moses do in righteous anger when he drew near the camp and saw the golden calf and the dancing?
options: He cast the two stone tablets out of his hands and broke them at the foot of the mountain
He surrendered his leadership to Aaron
He joined in the singing
He fled back up the mountain alone
questions.explanation: Moses’ anger became hot, and he cast the tablets out of his hands and broke them at the foot of the mountain (Exodus 32:19), signifying that the covenant had been shattered.

questions.text: What did Moses do to the golden calf to demonstrate the utter futility and powerlessness of man-made idols?
options: He buried it deep under the rocks of Sinai
He burned it in the fire, ground it to powder, scattered it on the water, and made the Israelites drink it
He shipped it back to Egypt
He hid it in the Ark of the Covenant
questions.explanation: Exodus 32:20: 'Then he took the calf which they had made, burned it in the fire, and ground it to powder; and he scattered it on the water and made the children of Israel drink it.'

questions.text: What feeble excuse did Aaron offer to Moses when questioned about how the idol was made?
options: The Egyptians forced me at swordpoint
The people are set on evil... I cast their gold into the fire, and out came this calf!
Joshua carved it while you were away
An angel appeared and ordered me to mold it
questions.explanation: Aaron shifted blame: 'You know the people, that they are set on evil... I cast it into the fire, and this calf came out' (Exodus 32:22-24).

questions.text: When Moses stood in the entrance of the camp and shouted 'Whoever is on the Lord's side—come to me!', which tribe gathered to him?
options: The tribe of Judah
All the sons of Levi
The tribe of Ephraim
The tribe of Benjamin
questions.explanation: Exodus 32:26: 'Then Moses stood in the entrance of the camp, and said, "Whoever is on the Lord’s side—come to me!" And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together to him.'

questions.text: How many rebellious men of Israel fell that day by the sword of the Levites executing divine judgment?
options: About 300 men
About 3,000 men
About 30,000 men
Only the elders
questions.explanation: Exodus 32:28: 'So the sons of Levi did according to the word of Moses. And about three thousand men of the people fell that day.'

questions.text: What remarkable sacrificial prayer of intercession did Moses offer for Israel in Exodus 32:32?
options: Lord, give me all their gold and silver
Yet now, if You will forgive their sin—but if not, I pray, blot me out of Your book which You have written!
Destroy only the women and spare the men
Let Aaron bear the penalty alone
questions.explanation: Moses demonstrated self-sacrificing leadership: 'Yet now, if You will forgive their sin—but if not, I pray, blot me out of Your book which You have written' (Exodus 32:32).

questions.text: How did God respond to Moses' request to be blotted out for the people's sin?
options: God agreed and took Moses' life
Whoever has sinned against Me, I will blot him out of My book
God blotted out the entire tribe of Levi
God gave up on the covenant completely
questions.explanation: The Lord replied: 'Whoever has sinned against Me, I will blot him out of My book' (Exodus 32:33), affirming individual moral accountability.

questions.text: In Deuteronomy 30:19, what clear choice did God present to the Israelites before entering the Promised Land?
options: Between gold and silver
I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing; therefore choose life, that both you and your descendants may live
Between living in tents or in palaces
Between fighting the Canaanites or retreating to Egypt
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 30:19: 'I call heaven and earth as witnesses today against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing; therefore choose life...'

questions.text: According to Deuteronomy 30:15-20, what is the key to enjoying long life and prosperity in the land?
options: Accumulating foreign trade alliances
Loving the Lord, walking in His ways, and keeping His commandments
Offering human sacrifices on high hills
Serving the gods of the Amorites secretly
questions.explanation: God promised that love, obedience, and clinging to Yahweh would bring life, blessing, and prolonged days in the land.

questions.text: Which prophet explicitly prophesied that God would make a 'New Covenant' with the house of Israel and the house of Judah?
options: Amos
Jeremiah (Jeremiah 31:31-34)
Hosea
Jonah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:31 declares: 'Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.'

questions.text: How does Jeremiah describe the nature of the New Covenant in contrast to the Sinai covenant?
options: It will be written on tablets of bronze
It will not be like the covenant broken by their fathers; God will put His law in their minds and write it on their hearts
It will require daily animal sacrifices on Mount Zion
It will only apply to people of royal blood
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:33: 'I will put My law in their minds, and write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be My people.'

questions.text: What universal spiritual knowledge is promised under the New Covenant in Jeremiah 31:34?
options: Only the priests will know Hebrew
No more shall every man teach his neighbor, saying, 'Know the Lord,' for they all shall know Me, from the least to the greatest
All wisdom will be kept in secret books
Prophecy will be abolished forever
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:34: 'No more shall every man teach his neighbor... saying, "Know the Lord," for they all shall know Me, from the least of them to the greatest of them.'

questions.text: What promise concerning sin concludes the New Covenant prophecy in Jeremiah 31:34?
options: Sinners will be cast into the sea
For I will forgive their iniquity, and their sin I will remember no more
Every sin must be repaid with twenty sheep
Sins will only be forgiven once every fifty years
questions.explanation: 'For I will forgive their iniquity, and their sin I will remember no more' (Jeremiah 31:34).

questions.text: According to Ezekiel 36:25, what cleansing action will God perform under the renewed covenant?
options: Wash their clothes in the river Jordan
Sprinkle clean water on you, and you shall be clean from all your filthiness and from all your idols
Burn their cities with fire
Exile them to Babylon forever
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:25: 'Then I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you shall be clean; I will cleanse you from all your filthiness and from all your idols.'

questions.text: What radical internal transformation does God promise to work in human nature in Ezekiel 36:26?
options: Give them angelic wings to fly
Give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you; take the heart of stone out of your flesh and give you a heart of flesh
Erase all their past memories
Make their physical bodies immortal immediately
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:26: 'I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you; I will take the heart of stone out of your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.'

questions.text: What will enable God's people to walk in His statutes according to Ezekiel 36:27?
options: Strict threats of physical punishment
I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My statutes, and you will keep My judgments and do them
A permanent army of Levites policing every home
Erecting stone monuments in every town
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:27 highlights the inner empowering work of the Holy Spirit: 'I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My statutes...'

questions.text: How did Jesus Christ institute and fulfill the New Covenant during the Last Supper (Luke 22:20)?
options: By carving new stone tablets
By taking the cup after supper, saying, 'This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is shed for you'
By sending His disciples to buy sheep in the market
By washing His hands in water like Pilate
questions.explanation: Luke 22:20: 'Likewise He also took the cup after supper, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is shed for you."'

questions.text: What is a primary distinction between the Sinai (Old) Covenant and the New Covenant in Christ?
options: The Old was written on stone tablets and focused on external letter and ceremonial law, while the New is written on hearts by the Spirit and based on grace and redemption
The Old applied to all nations, whereas the New applies only to Jerusalem
The Old had no commandments against murder
The New abolished all need for love and faith
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3 and Hebrews 8 contrast the external, ceremonial letter of the Sinai covenant with the internal, spiritual life and forgiveness of the New Covenant.

questions.text: How has modern society often broken God's covenant today according to Christian teaching?
options: By advancing medical technology
By rampant materialism, moral laxity, corruption, injustice, and turning away from God's holy standards
By reading biblical history
By building larger church buildings
questions.explanation: Contemporary society breaks covenant through widespread materialism, unfaithfulness, injustice, profaning God's name, and disobedience.

questions.text: The concept of 'circumcision of the heart' emphasized by Jeremiah and the New Testament signifies:
options: A physical surgical operation on the chest
Inward spiritual purification, genuine repentance, and complete devotion of the inner man to God
Refusal to participate in civic governance
Memorizing the genealogy of kings
questions.explanation: Circumcision of the heart refers to the internal transformation of desires, affections, and will toward God, beyond mere external ritual.

questions.text: Why was the sin of the golden calf considered such a grave betrayal by Israel?
options: Gold was too expensive to waste
They had just witnessed God's awesome holiness on Sinai and solemnly vowed 'All that the Lord has spoken we will do', yet quickly violated the very first two commandments
Aaron was not an artist
The calf had no horns
questions.explanation: Israel flagrantly broke their freshly sworn covenant before the smoke had even cleared from Sinai, committing spiritual adultery.

questions.text: What role did Moses fulfill during the golden calf episode that typifies the ministry of Jesus Christ?
options: A military general conquering Egypt
A faithful mediator and intercessor pleading for mercy on behalf of guilty people
A tax collector for the sanctuary
A judge sentencing everyone to exile
questions.explanation: Moses stood in the breach as mediator, averting divine wrath, prefiguring Christ who ever lives to make intercession for us (Hebrews 7:25).

questions.text: What happened when God renewed the broken covenant tablets in Exodus 34?
options: God commanded Moses to cut two stone tablets like the first ones, and God wrote upon them the words of the Ten Commandments
God refused to give any written law again
Aaron was given bronze tablets instead
The angels brought golden tablets down from heaven
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:1: 'The Lord said to Moses, "Cut two tablets of stone like the first ones, and I will write on these tablets the words that were on the first tablets which you broke."'

questions.text: What remarkable physical transformation occurred on Moses' face after spending forty days on Mount Sinai receiving the renewed covenant?
options: His skin turned pale gray
The skin of his face shone brightly with divine glory so that he had to put on a veil
He lost his eyesight completely
His beard turned into gold
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:29-35 records that the skin of Moses' face shone because he had been talking with God, causing the people to be afraid, so he put a veil over his face.

questions.text: In Jeremiah 32:38-40, God promises to give His people 'one heart and one way' so that:
options: They may speak only one dialect
They may fear Me forever, for their good and the good of their children after them, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them
They will never engage in agriculture again
They will build a single great city
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:39-40: 'Then I will give them one heart and one way, that they may fear Me forever, for the good of them and their children after them...'

questions.text: How does the New Covenant offer reconciliation to all humanity beyond national Israel?
options: It requires everyone to adopt Jewish civic laws
Through faith in Jesus Christ, the dividing wall of hostility is broken, making Gentiles and Jews fellow citizens and members of God's household
It excludes non-Hebrew speakers from salvation
It makes Jerusalem the mandatory residence of all Christians
questions.explanation: Ephesians 2:13-19 and Galatians 3:28 declare that in Christ Jesus, salvation is universally available to all nations by faith.

questions.text: What warning does the incident of the golden calf provide to religious leaders today?
options: Never allow jewelry in the community
Leaders must never compromise divine truth or yield to popular, sinful pressure to accommodate idols
Leaders should always remain on high mountains
Elders must not delegate tasks to anyone
questions.explanation: Aaron's tragic failure shows that leaders who succumb to public fear and popular demand lead their followers into destruction.

questions.text: What theological truth is emphasized by God sending plagues on Israel after the golden calf idolatry (Exodus 32:35)?
options: God forgives but also disciplines His people to teach the holiness of His name and the gravity of sin
Plagues happen strictly by accident in the wilderness
Moses had no influence with God
Idolatry is overlooked by God after sacrifices are offered
questions.explanation: God in His mercy spared the nation from total extinction, but in His holy justice disciplined the unrepentant rebels.

questions.text: Which book of the Old Testament repeatedly emphasizes the blessings of obedience and curses of disobedience for the covenant people?
options: Deuteronomy
Esther
Song of Solomon
Ecclesiastes
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy (especially chapters 28 and 30) articulates the covenantal blessings of obedience and curses of disobedience.

questions.text: What does the 'blood of the New Covenant' shed on Calvary accomplish according to Hebrews 9:14?
options: It serves only as a symbolic reminder like animal blood
It cleanses our conscience from dead works to serve the living God
It only forgives sins committed before the flood
It purchases earthly property in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Hebrews 9:14: 'how much more shall the blood of Christ... cleanse your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?'

questions.text: In the New Covenant, who serves as the sole Mediator between God and mankind?
options: Moses
The Levitical high priest
Jesus Christ, the Son of God
The prophet Jeremiah
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 2:5: 'For there is one God and one Mediator between God and men, the Man Christ Jesus.'

questions.text: What attribute of God's character was proclaimed to Moses on Mount Sinai in Exodus 34:6-7?
options: A distant and silent cosmic force
The Lord, the Lord God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abounding in goodness and truth
A harsh judge without compassion
A deity who changes His mind daily
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:6: 'The Lord, the Lord God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abounding in goodness and truth, keeping mercy for thousands...'

questions.text: Under the New Covenant, how is a believer justified and declared righteous before God?
options: By perfect adherence to every ceremonial feast of the law
By grace through faith in Jesus Christ, apart from works of the law
By purchasing sacrificial lambs in the temple
By genealogical descent from Abraham
questions.explanation: Romans 3:28: 'Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith apart from the deeds of the law.'

questions.text: What was the significance of the Tabernacle constructed by Israel following the renewal of the covenant?
options: A fortress to store captured weapons
A sacred dwelling place where God's glory dwelt in the midst of His redeemed people
A commercial bank for gold and silver
A hotel for traveling Egyptian ambassadors
questions.explanation: Exodus 25:8: 'And let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them.'

questions.text: In Ezekiel's prophecy, replacing the 'heart of stone' with a 'heart of flesh' illustrates:
options: A biological organ transplant
Regeneration and spiritual transformation, turning hardened, insensitive souls into responsive, tender lovers of God
Physical weakness and loss of courage
A return to Egyptian rituals
questions.explanation: The stony heart represents stubborn spiritual rebellion, while the heart of flesh signifies a repentant, soft, and obedient spirit.

questions.text: Why did the old Sinai covenant need to be superseded by the New Covenant according to Hebrews 8:7-8?
options: Because the Ten Commandments contained moral errors
Because the people did not remain faithful to that covenant and were unable in human weakness to keep its terms
Because Moses did not build the altar correctly
Because Mount Sinai collapsed
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:7-8 notes that finding fault with the people's ability to keep the law, God declared the New Covenant based on better promises and internal grace.

questions.text: How should a Christian maintain faithfulness to the New Covenant in everyday living?
options: By living in obedience to Christ's teachings, loving one another, and walking daily in the power of the Holy Spirit
By isolating oneself from all human society permanently
By seeking revenge against persecutors
By offering animal sacrifices on Sundays
questions.explanation: Covenant faithfulness in the New Testament is marked by love, holiness, bearing the fruit of the Spirit, and obedience to Christ.

questions.text: What permanent feast did Jesus give His followers to celebrate their participation in the New Covenant?
options: The Feast of Tabernacles
The Holy Communion (Lord's Supper / Eucharist)
The Feast of Purim
The Jubilee Year trumpet
questions.explanation: The Lord's Supper commemorates Christ's broken body and the blood of the New Covenant poured out for the remission of sins (1 Corinthians 11:23-26).

questions.text: In biblical theology, what is the ultimate eternal dwelling of the redeemed under the New Covenant described in Revelation 21?
options: An earthly palace in Babylon
The New Jerusalem, where God Himself will be with them and be their God, wiping away every tear
The Garden of Eden guarded by cherubim
A kingdom of military chariots
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:3: 'Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and He will dwell with them, and they shall be His people. God Himself will be with them and be their God.'

questions.text: Which of the following best summarizes the progression of covenants from Noah to Christ?
options: From preservation of creation (Noah), to election of a family of faith (Abraham), to national holy law (Sinai), to universal spiritual redemption and eternal life (Christ)
From monarchy to democracy and then to empire
From strict animal vegetarianism to temple taxation
From wandering nomadism to commercial trading
questions.explanation: Redemptive history moves seamlessly from cosmic preservation (Noah), to personal/familial faith (Abraham), to national identity (Sinai), culminating in universal redemption through Christ.

questions.text: How many sons did the patriarch Jacob have, who later became the fathers of the twelve tribes of Israel?
options: Seven sons
Ten sons
Twelve sons
Fourteen sons
questions.explanation: Jacob had twelve sons born to him by Leah, Rachel, Bilhah, and Zilpah (Genesis 35:22-26).

questions.text: Who was the mother of Joseph, Jacob's beloved and second wife?
options: Leah
Rachel
Bilhah
Zilpah
questions.explanation: Joseph was the firstborn son of Rachel, Jacob's deeply loved wife (Genesis 30:22-24).

questions.text: Why did Jacob love Joseph more than all his other sons?
options: Because Joseph was the oldest of all the brothers
Because Joseph was the son of his old age
Because Joseph had conquered surrounding tribes
Because Joseph gave him the most cattle
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:3: 'Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age.'

questions.text: What special garment did Jacob make for Joseph that provoked intense jealousy among his brothers?
options: A military breastplate of bronze
A coat of many colors (tunic of diverse colors / ornamented robe)
A linen priest's turban
A shepherd's leather cloak
questions.explanation: Jacob made Joseph a tunic of many colors (Genesis 37:3), signifying special favoritism and heirship.

questions.text: What was the subject of Joseph's first prophetic dream in Genesis 37:7?
options: Seven cows coming out of the river
Binding sheaves in the field, and his sheaf arose while his brothers' sheaves bowed down to it
Birds devouring loaves of bread from a basket
Stars falling from heaven onto the mountains
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:7: 'There we were, binding sheaves in the field. Then behold, my sheaf arose and also stood upright; and indeed your sheaves stood round about and bowed down to my sheaf.'

questions.text: What was the subject of Joseph's second dream in Genesis 37:9?
options: Seven plump heads of wheat swallowing thin heads
The sun, the moon, and eleven stars making obeisance to him
An eagle flying over Egypt
Twelve chariots of fire
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:9: 'Look, I have dreamed another dream. And this time, the sun, the moon, and the eleven stars bowed down to me.'

questions.text: How did Jacob respond when Joseph narrated his second dream involving the sun, moon, and eleven stars?
options: He promoted Joseph immediately to family judge
He rebuked him and said, 'Shall I and your mother and your brothers indeed come to bow down to the earth before you?' but kept the saying in mind
He cast Joseph out of the house
He sold his cattle in anger
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:10-11: Jacob rebuked him, yet his father kept the matter in mind, while his brothers envied him.

questions.text: Where did Jacob initially send seventeen-year-old Joseph to check on the welfare of his brothers and the flocks?
options: To Jerusalem
To Shechem
To Beersheba
To Jericho
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:13-14: Jacob sent Joseph from the Valley of Hebron to Shechem where his brothers were pasturing the flock.

questions.text: Where did a wandering stranger inform Joseph that his brothers had moved to?
options: Bethel
Dothan
Gilead
Shiloh
questions.explanation: The man said, 'They have departed from here, for I heard them say, "Let us go to Dothan."' So Joseph found them in Dothan (Genesis 37:17).

questions.text: What wicked conspiracy did Joseph's brothers form when they saw him approaching in the distance at Dothan?
options: Let us welcome him and prepare a feast
Look, this dreamer is coming! Come therefore, let us now kill him and cast him into some pit... and we shall see what will become of his dreams!
Let us ask him to interpret our father's dreams
Let us flee to Egypt before he arrives
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:19-20: 'They said to one another, "Look, this dreamer is coming! Come therefore, let us now kill him and cast him into some pit..."'

questions.text: Which brother intervened to save Joseph's life, suggesting they throw him into an empty cistern rather than shed his blood?
options: Simeon
Reuben, the firstborn
Judah
Levi
questions.explanation: Reuben heard it and delivered him out of their hands, intending to rescue him later and deliver him back to his father (Genesis 37:21-22).

questions.text: While Reuben was absent, which brother proposed selling Joseph to the passing Ishmaelite/Midianite merchants instead of letting him die?
options: Dan
Judah
Naphtali
Gad
questions.explanation: Judah said to his brothers: 'What profit is there if we kill our brother and conceal his blood? Come and let us sell him to the Ishmaelites' (Genesis 37:26-27).

questions.text: For how much silver was Joseph sold by his brothers to the Ishmaelite traders?
options: Ten shekels of silver
Twenty shekels of silver
Thirty pieces of silver
Fifty shekels of silver
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:28: 'Then Midianite traders passed by; so the brothers pulled Joseph up and lifted him out of the pit, and sold him to the Ishmaelites for twenty shekels of silver.'

questions.text: How did the brothers deceive their father Jacob regarding Joseph's disappearance?
options: They claimed Joseph had drowned in the Jordan
They slaughtered a kid of the goats, dipped Joseph's tunic of many colors in the blood, and brought it to their father
They said Joseph had decided to join an Egyptian caravan voluntarily
They blamed a band of Philistine robbers
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:31-33: They dipped the coat in goat's blood, and Jacob recognized it, weeping: 'It is my son’s tunic. A wild beast has devoured him. Without doubt Joseph is torn to pieces.'

questions.text: To whom in Egypt was Joseph sold as a slave upon arrival?
options: To Pharaoh directly
To Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard
To the chief baker of the royal bakery
To an Egyptian grain merchant in Thebes
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:36; 39:1: 'Now Joseph had been taken down to Egypt. And Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him...'

questions.text: Why did Potiphar make Joseph overseer over his house and all that he possessed?
options: Because Joseph was skilled in military warfare
Because Potiphar saw that the Lord was with Joseph and that the Lord made all he did to prosper
Because Joseph paid him twenty pieces of gold
Because Pharaoh commanded it
questions.explanation: Genesis 39:3-4: 'And his master saw that the Lord was with him and that the Lord made all he did to prosper in his hand. So Joseph found favor in his sight...'

questions.text: What moral trial confronted Joseph in the house of Potiphar, and how did he respond?
options: He was tempted to steal gold, but gave it to the poor
